radio_rulings.claim: What is the Zero W Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip called?

sides.claim: Cypress CYW43438, the same combo chip as Raspberry Pi 3 Model B.

sources.section: Launch blog, 28 Feb 2017: 'It uses the same Cypress CYW43438 wireless chip as Raspberry Pi 3 Model B'
Cypress (2017) press release announcing CYW43438 on Raspberry Pi Zero W

sides.claim: BCM43438 and CYW43438 are the same device; only the prefix changed after Cypress acquired Broadcom's IoT line.

sources.section: Cypress/Infineon part-number mapping table: BCM43438 = CYW43438, 'no change in form, fit, or function'

sides.claim: Some secondary articles call the chip BCM43143.

sources.section: Magazine article that equates BCM43143 with CYW43438; this is a misidentification of a different Broadcom part.

radio_rulings.ruling: The chip is Cypress/Infineon CYW43438, also marked BCM43438 on some boards. These two names are the same silicon. BCM43143 is a different part and is not used as the official identity of the Zero W radio.
radio_rulings.prefer: Official launch blog, official Cypress announcement, and the vendor mapping table, over magazine/secondary part-number mix-ups.

radio_rulings.claim: Is the Zero W Bluetooth 4.0, 4.1, or 5.1?

sources.section: Official product specification: 'Bluetooth 4.1' and 'Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)'
Cypress 2017 PR: CYW43438 enables 'simultaneous Bluetooth 4.1 operations' and BLE on Zero W
Feature changes from Raspberry Pi Zero: 'Bluetooth 4.0 and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)'

sides.claim: The current CYW43438 silicon family is qualified to Bluetooth 5.1.

sources.section: Current Infineon datasheet: 'Qualified for Bluetooth Core Specification 5.1 compliance'

radio_rulings.ruling: Treat the Zero W product specification as Bluetooth 4.1 + BLE. That is what the official product page and the contemporary Cypress announcement say. The 'Bluetooth 4.0' wording on the 2017 blog and on the current Zero documentation 'feature changes' section disagrees with the product page and is treated as a documentation inconsistency, not a second SKU. The later Infineon '5.1 compliance' statement describes a subsequent qualification of the chip family; it is not a Raspberry Pi product claim for Zero W firmware or a guarantee of Bluetooth 5.1 features on this board.
radio_rulings.prefer: Official product specification page and the 2017 Cypress PR over the launch-blog bullet list, the Zero documentation feature-changes paragraph, and later chip-family marketing.

radio_rulings.claim: Does Zero W support 802.11ac or 5 GHz Wi-Fi?

sources.section: Official product specification: '802.11 b/g/n wireless LAN'
Datasheet body: 'Single-band 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.11b/g/n' and a single shared 2.4 GHz antenna
A datasheet title/filename variant has used '802.11ac' wording, but the body specifies 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n only.

radio_rulings.ruling: Zero W is 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n only. It does not have 5 GHz or 802.11ac. Prefer the official product specification and the datasheet body over any 'ac' wording in a vendor title.
radio_rulings.prefer: Official product brief and datasheet body.

notes: This dataset is for the original Raspberry Pi Zero W (BCM2835, 2017), not Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (RP3A0).
All board coordinates use millimetres, origin at the bottom-left corner of the PCB, top view of the component side. Left = microSD + mini-HDMI; right = CSI; GPIO at the top; HDMI/USB at the bottom.
header_state_default is bare-pads: Zero W ships with an unpopulated 40-pin header footprint.

microSD is on the left short edge (official 16.9 mm y-centre-line; drawn footprint measured on RP-008367-DS). CSI is on the right short edge (official 15 mm y-centre-line; housing measured on RP-008367-DS).

The 2.4 GHz antenna is described officially as a Proant Niche PCB cavity between mini-HDMI and USB OTG, but it is not outlined on the RP-008367-DS assembly drawing, so its bounding box is null (suspect / not drawn). The unlabeled 9.64 mm dimension is not the antenna.
ACT LED identity is confirmed from the schematic (D2 green 1611); its coordinates are null because they are not labelled on the mechanical drawing and were not uniquely identified on photographs.
Where RP-008367-DS does not dimension a part, x/y/w/h are null with a note. Values are never invented.
Footprint boxes for mini-HDMI and the two micro-USB connectors include the small overhang past the board edge (negative y).
